chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-Amriki from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) from his father (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) said:

Regarding a man who marries a woman on the condition of a slave girl (waseef), and she grows old in her possession, and he wishes to divorce her before consummating the marriage with her, he said: 'Upon him is half the value of the day he delivered her to her; no regard is given to increase or decrease.'

key_terms.وَصِيفٍ: A slave girl or concubine, often used as part of the dowry or possession in classical fiqh

ai.seo_question: What is the dowry ruling if a man divorces his wife before consummation when the marriage was based on a slave girl?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Musa al-Kazim clarifies the financial settlement (mahr) when a husband divorces before consummation, specifically addressing the valuation of a 'waseef' (slave concubine) provided as part of the dowry. The Imam establishes that the compensation is fixed at half the value on the day of delivery, explicitly excluding fluctuations in price, which reflects the Shia juristic principle of stabilizing financial obligations at the time of transfer. This hadith is significant in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for illustrating how pre-Islamic and early Islamic customs regarding slave concubines were integrated into Islamic family law with precise jurisprudential adjustments.
